newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--All-night negotiations between three ministers and the representatives of striking seamen have brought hope for an end to the 11-day strike. Talks with teachers have also brought optimism for a resolution. The 24-hour General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) strike, however, will go ahead as planned today.
--The national economy ministry is warning public utilities and organisations that excessive spending on wages - overshooting budgets by 80 percent last year - will not be tolerated.

--"Whoever laughs last, laughs best," Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis said yesterday, his response to comments by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou over the withdrawal of the licence for the Athens casino.
--A bridge has been built with the seamen and a step take towards teachers: the possibility of a resolution is in sight for both fronts.

--Late last night, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou tried to temper her comments about Laliotis, saying he was the one who did all he could to throw light on illegality. Her comments came after a scathing intervention from Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
--A revolutionary new cigarette filter has drawn international interest and will go on sale on February 1. The Greek inventors of the filter presented it to the press yesterday.
--After secretive back stage meetings, the government managed to put together a new improved proposal for seamen, presented to them last night.
--A bitter end to the tragedy of the 283 illegal immigrants drowned in the Mediterranean: the survivors who revealed the tragedy - of which authorities there is still no evidence - are deported.
--A woman who gave birth to a girl was given a boy, discovering the mistake only hours after she took the baby home. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
